newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares break winning streak, end lower.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares break winning streak, end lower.

text.p: Dutch shares finished lower on Wednesday, bringing a five-session run of record high closings to an end as investors took profits on a low volume day.

Dealers pointed out that prices in the AEX share index had not moved particularly dramatically but had been drifting and were dragged lower by big falls in a couple of stocks. "It's just profit-taking. If you look outside Philips and Aegon not much has happened today," one dealer said.
The AEX share index closed 3.62 points lower at 827.15 after probing up to 831.59 early in the session. Dealers say charts point to 850 as a near-term AEX resistance level.

"There are a lot of private investors in this market and some of them are taking profits," said another dealer, adding the market was happy to ignore gains on Wall Street, where the Dow had added 61 points on Tuesday and rose again on Wednesday.
"The U.S. has been going up so far so fast now it's becoming a bit unreal," he said. "When you see gains of hundreds of points over a few days people don't look at it any more."

"This is just a pause for breath," said another dealer. "Underlying fundamentals of low inflation and corporate growth are still there," he added. "The index could go up to 850, 875 or higher, there's a good basis," said another.

Dealers said some players were hanging back from the market ahead of next week's Amsterdam EU summit at which tough talking is expected on the stability pact aimed at enforcing budgetary restraint during economic and monetary union (EMU).
Speculation has emerged the pact could be watered down by France after socialists won France's recent general election.
Incoming Dutch central bank head Arnout Wellink touched a raw nerve when he told a conference in Amsterdam on Wednesday that agreement on the stability pact next week was not certain.
"It's not that anyone here really thinks EMU isn't going to happen, it's...markets don't like uncertainty," a dealer said.
